body: Sensex peaked at ~6,150 intraday on 11 Feb 2000 (level from memory; not confirmed in sources found) and fell to ~2,600 by Sept 2001 (post-9/11 low) - roughly -58%. What led: 'ICE' (information technology, communications, entertainment) and Ketan Parekh's 'K-10' stocks - Zee Telefilms (reportedly ~Rs 127 to ~Rs 10,000 pre-split), HFCL, Global Tele-Systems, DSQ Software, Pentamedia, Aftek, Silverline. Parekh funded positions via Madhavpura Mercantile Cooperative Bank and Global Trust Bank, plus 'badla' carry-forward financing. In the two months after April 2000, K-10 stocks fell ~67% vs -23% for the Sensex (student document; weak source); for the year to Feb 2002 the K-10 averaged -51.7% vs -16% for the Sensex (Business Standard). A bear-cartel raid and the Feb 2001 budget triggered the March 2001 crash; MMCB collapsed, UTI's US-64 froze (July 2001), badla was banned and rolling settlement introduced. What lagged: 'old economy' stocks that traded at single-digit P/Es (unverified levels). Valuation at peak: Sensex P/E ~28-35x depending on source (28x, 29x, ~35x Apr 2000). Top signals: extreme concentration in one theme, cooperative-bank funding of a broker, triple-digit P/Es on IT names. Lesson: many K-10 names never recovered; theme leaders of one bubble rarely lead the next.
title: Ketan Parekh and the ICE/tech bubble (1999-2001)
